### Contributing guidelines

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [x] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version of the `main` branch

### Module(s)

mini.files

### Neovim version

0.13 (!at least latest Nightly build!)

### Description

> **Edit:** see the maintainer's comment below — a server sending explicit
> `null` for `fileOperationFilter.scheme` is non-conformant per the LSP spec
> (unlike fields that explicitly allow `| null`), so this is not a bug in
> `mini.files`. Left the report here for reference and corrected the one
> inaccurate claim below (the `matches` field is *not* affected). The
> "Suggested fix" section is withdrawn.

Creating/deleting/renaming a file in `mini.files` crashes when an attached LSP
client declares a `fileOperationFilter` with `"scheme": null` instead of omitting
the field:

```
E5108: Lua: .../mini.nvim/lua/mini/files.lua:2862: attempt to concatenate local 'scheme' (a userdata value)
stack traceback:
        .../mini.nvim/lua/mini/files.lua:2862: in function 'is_scheme'
        .../mini.nvim/lua/mini/files.lua:2870: in function 'filt'
        .../mini.nvim/lua/mini/files.lua:2892: in function 'lsp_fs_hook_client'
        .../mini.nvim/lua/mini/files.lua:2853: in function 'lsp_fs_hook'
        .../mini.nvim/lua/mini/files.lua:2816: in function 'fs_actions_apply'
        .../mini.nvim/lua/mini/files.lua:865: in function <.../mini.nvim/lua/mini/files.lua:855>
E5108: Lua: .../mini.nvim/lua/mini/files.lua:2862: attempt to concatenate local 'scheme' (a userdata value)
stack traceback:
        .../mini.nvim/lua/mini/files.lua:2862: in function 'is_scheme'
        .../mini.nvim/lua/mini/files.lua:2870: in function 'filt'
        .../mini.nvim/lua/mini/files.lua:2892: in function 'lsp_fs_hook_client'
        .../mini.nvim/lua/mini/files.lua:2853: in function 'lsp_fs_hook'
        .../mini.nvim/lua/mini/files.lua:2818: in function 'fs_actions_apply'
        .../mini.nvim/lua/mini/files.lua:865: in function <.../mini.nvim/lua/mini/files.lua:855>
```

It throws twice: once from the `didCreate` hook (`fs_actions_apply:2816`) and
once from `didRename` (`fs_actions_apply:2818`).

Neovim decodes JSON `null` into `vim.NIL` (a userdata sentinel), not Lua `nil`.
The `scheme == nil` check in `H.lsp_fs_hook_client` does not catch it, so
execution falls through to `scheme .. ':'` and throws:

```lua
-- lua/mini/files.lua:2862
local is_scheme = function(uri, scheme) return scheme == nil or vim.startswith(uri, scheme .. ':') end
```

### Real-world server that triggers this

[`markdown-oxide`](https://github.com/Feel-ix-343/markdown-oxide) (v0.25.9)
sends `"scheme": null` in its `fileOperationFilter` (`matches` is correctly
omitted, not affected — see edit note above):

https://github.com/Feel-ix-343/markdown-oxide/blob/main/src/main.rs#L403-L413

```rust
let file_op_reg = FileOperationRegistrationOptions {
    filters: std::iter::once(FileOperationFilter {
        pattern: FileOperationPattern { options: None, glob: "**/*.md".into(), matches: None },
        ..Default::default()   // <- scheme: None  =>  "scheme": null on the wire
    })
    .collect(),
};
```

The root cause is in the `lsp-types` crate `markdown-oxide` depends on:
`FileOperationFilter::scheme` is the only optional field in that struct
missing `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`, while
`FileOperationPattern`'s `matches` and `options` both have it — so `None`
serializes to explicit `null` instead of being omitted. Still the case as of
`lsp-types` 0.97.0. Will file upstream against `lsp-types` and
`markdown-oxide` separately.

It registers this for `did_create` / `did_rename` / `did_delete`, so creating any
`.md` file in `mini.files` with `markdown-oxide` attached crashes reliably.

### Reproduction

Self-contained; needs no external LSP server. The mock below emulates exactly what
`markdown-oxide` puts on the wire — `vim.NIL` is what Neovim's JSON decoder
produces for `null`, so passing it directly is a faithful stand-in.

1. Create separate 'nvim-repro' config directory:
    - '~/.config/nvim-repro/' on Unix
    - '~/AppData/Local/nvim-repro/' on Windows

2. Inside 'nvim-repro' directory create a file named 'init.lua'.
   Populate it with the following content:

    ```lua
    -- Clone latest 'mini.nvim' (requires Git CLI installed)
    vim.cmd('echo "Installing `mini.nvim`" | redraw')
    local mini_path = vim.fn.stdpath('data') .. '/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim'
    local clone_cmd = { 'git', 'clone', '--depth=1', 'https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim', mini_path }
    vim.fn.system(clone_cmd)
    vim.cmd('echo "`mini.nvim` is installed" | redraw')

    -- Make sure 'mini.nvim' is available
    vim.cmd('packadd mini.nvim')
    require('mini.deps').setup()

    require('mini.files').setup()

    -- Minimal in-process LSP server that declares `scheme = null` in its
    -- `fileOperationFilter`, the way 'markdown-oxide' does.
    -- `vim.NIL` is what Neovim's JSON decoder produces for `null`.
    local filters = { { pattern = { glob = '**' }, scheme = vim.NIL } }
    local capabilities = {
      workspace = { fileOperations = { didCreate = { filters = filters } } },
    }

    local cmd = function(_)
      local is_closing, request_id = false, 0
      return {
        request = function(method, _, callback)
          if method == 'initialize' then callback(nil, { capabilities = capabilities }) end
          if method == 'shutdown' then callback(nil, nil) end
          request_id = request_id + 1
          return true, request_id
        end,
        notify = function() return true end,
        is_closing = function() return is_closing end,
        terminate = function() is_closing = true end,
      }
    end

    vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('BufEnter', {
      callback = function() vim.lsp.start({ name = 'null-scheme-lsp', cmd = cmd, root_dir = vim.fn.getcwd() }) end,
    })
    ```

3. Run `NVIM_APPNAME=nvim-repro nvim` (i.e. execute `nvim` with `NVIM_APPNAME`
   environment variable set to "nvim-repro"). Wait for all dependencies to install.

4. Open some file so that the mock server attaches (`:lua =vim.lsp.get_clients()`
   should list `null-scheme-lsp`).

5. Run `:lua MiniFiles.open()`, type `o`, enter a new file name, press `<Esc>`, and
   synchronize with `=`. Confirm the action.

6. Observe the crash:
   `E5108: Lua: .../mini/files.lua:2862: attempt to concatenate local 'scheme' (a userdata value)`

comment_data.body:
Thanks for the issue!

> Per the LSP spec, both `scheme` and `pattern.matches` are optional; an absent
> value means "match anything". A server sending explicit `null` should be treated
> the same as omitting the field, rather than crashing (`scheme`) or matching
> nothing (`matches`).

I don't think this is how LSP specification works. And definitely not how Neovim itself interprets it since 0.12.0 (when explicit `null` began to be treated differently from the missing field).

The spec defines that [`fileOperationFilter`](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#fileOperationFilter) can have only missing values and no `null`. There are many instances where `null` is listed explicitly as an allowed value and only in that case `vim.NIL` on Neovim side is treated as a valid value.

For the time being, the server sending `null` as a value for the field that does not explicitly list `null` as an allowed value is treated as an upstream server issue. Please open an issue upstream to hopefully have it resolved there.

Until this is resolved, to continue using 'mini.files' without interruptions disabling LSP integrations with`config.options.lsp_timeout = 0` should help.

Thanks for the quick response — you're right, and I withdraw the suggestion.

Re-reading the spec: `fileOperationFilter` declares `scheme?: string`, and the
spec spells out `| null` explicitly wherever `null` is actually a permitted
value. So a server sending `"scheme": null` is simply non-conformant, and it
isn't `mini.files`'s job to paper over that. Agreed.

I also need to correct a factual error in my report. I claimed `markdown-oxide`
sends `"matches": null` as well — that was wrong. I inferred it from its
`..Default::default()` instead of checking, which I should not have done. Here is
what it actually puts on the wire:

```lua
-- client.server_capabilities.workspace.fileOperations.didCreate.filters[1]
{ pattern = { glob = "**/*.md" }, scheme = vim.NIL }
```

`matches` is correctly omitted; only `scheme` is `null`. So the `is_fs_type()`
half of my report was purely theoretical with no known server triggering it —
please disregard that part (I've edited the issue body above to remove it).
Sorry for the noise.

For the record, the root cause is not in `markdown-oxide`'s own code but in the
`lsp-types` crate it depends on: `FileOperationFilter::scheme` is the only
optional field in that struct missing
`#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`, while `FileOperationPattern`'s
`matches` and `options` both have it. This is still the case in the latest 0.97.0.
I'll report it there, and to `markdown-oxide` (which pins an older `lsp-types` via
a `tower-lsp` fork, so it needs its own fix regardless).

Thanks for the `lsp_timeout = 0` pointer. For anyone else landing here from the
same crash: a narrower workaround that keeps the LSP integration working for
well-behaved servers is to sanitize the offending capability in that client's own
`on_init`:

```lua
on_init = function(client)
  local file_ops = vim.tbl_get(client.server_capabilities, 'workspace', 'fileOperations')
  if type(file_ops) ~= 'table' then return end
  for _, reg in pairs(file_ops) do
    for _, filter in ipairs(type(reg) == 'table' and reg.filters or {}) do
      if filter.scheme == vim.NIL then filter.scheme = nil end
    end
  end
end,
```

Feel free to close.

title: mini.files: crash when LSP server sends `null` in `fileOperationFilter`
